svg.text: ORCA pulls the geological risk sectors that CPRM/SGB publishes for all 27
states and crosses each one with the rain that fell on it, flagging anything
past a threshold you drag along a ruler. Rain is hourly Open-Meteo per
coordinate, off one national query grid sized by binary search so the whole
country fits in the free daily request budget, and it sketches where alerts
are heading 72h out. The dashboard is static HTML and JS on GitHub Pages,
rebuilt every day: risk grade drawn as hatching like a geological map, live
INMET warnings, radar and lightning layers, CSV and PDF export, and you can
drop in your own area (GeoJSON, KML or shapefile) without it leaving the
browser. Rain is modeled, not gauged, and the 100mm default comes from the
literature, not an official calibration. A side project on public data, not a
warning system anyone should rely on.
